blocking.issue: Regression in a sibling path the fixer reported as covered (validation rule 8). The loop's abort branch now emits model_call_end with stopReason "error". The chat agent's SentenceGate reads every model_call_end as "the call ended normally" unless stopReason is "max_tokens". So a spoken turn (voice or phone) whose model call is cut off by its turn timeout now sends its held, unfinished sentence to the speaker. Before the fix it was dropped. This breaks the rule that a broken sentence is never spoken (real-audio run of 2026-10-26; conversation/agent.ts comment above the gate; conversation-sentences tests). The chat run is `protected`, so Stop all does not abort it: the timeout is the path. With the real API, message_start always carries usage, so callCost > 0 and the event always fires.
blocking.where: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:773 (new model_call_end in the abort branch) with packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:985-986 (`gate?.end(ev.stopReason === "max_tokens")`)
blocking.evidence:
Scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9d17d664-b8c3-5e0d-8f13-1f917f72dcc2/scratchpad/walk/aborted-spoken-chat.test.ts. It uses conversation.test.ts's setup() with a provider that sends message_start usage and the text "You have a decision waiting. The critic asked for one of the three options: adopt,", then waits for abort. The test runs a voice turn and advances the clock past the turn timeout.
- At 217902c it FAILS: onToken got ["You have a decision waiting. ","The critic asked for one of the three options: adopt,"], and the reply was "I could not answer (run timeout)."
- With the base loop.ts restored it PASSES: onToken got only ["You have a decision waiting. "].

I ran it in packages/runtime/test and then removed it; the worktree is clean.
blocking.expected: A call cut off by a stop or a timeout drops the held rest of a spoken turn, as it did before. For example, in agent.ts: `gate?.end(ev.stopReason === "max_tokens" || ev.stopReason === "error")`; that line is not in l3-chat-claims' owned regions (history, reply guard). The alternative is a stop reason the gate already treats as cut. Add a failing-first case to conversation.test.ts (a spoken turn cut off by its timeout streams no broken tail), then check the other model_call_end readers: intake's ttft, executor and runner booking.

non_blocking: The 'The critic started …' line is now emitted at the critic run's first model_call_start. In loop/critic.ts the marker checks and the sandbox tries (build, tests, tried pages) run before review(). So for a review with checks, the log shows nothing between "The coder finished …" and the start line while those run. Before, the line came first. Consider firing onStarted once the checks start, and still never on a refusal.

Seen on the bench (walk-budget-e/f/g): a session whose only task was done but cost more than planned read "Session review: sent back for changes (grade 85, 1 finding)." Nothing was sent back. The fixer lists this in new_problems; it belongs to a words area.

Overrun finding wording for several retries: ", with N more attempts of tasks tried again" reads awkwardly. Something like ", with 3 tasks tried again" or "with 3 more tries" reads better (design §5 plain words).

On the questions session, the session result (not this area) reads '"Contact page in contact.html" needs your decision (Inbox).' while the new review line says "waits for your answers". The two words for one fact differ; worth aligning in the result words' area.
Out of this area: on a session page opened directly (/sessions/:id), the shell's project picker kept showing the previous project ("Quote page ▾" over the "Notes stop" session).
